batch_strategy: Supplement the pending 16 with targeted tests of endpoint-specific solvent responses, a corrected follow-up to the m177 anomaly, connected carbonyl and alcohol comparisons, an acid response pair, and two structurally novel probes. Freeze all pending and selected IDs and their exact supplied predictions before measurement; predictions quoted below are rounded only for readability.

choices.reason: Measure m177 at 10/1, 150 uL, predicted 4.41/22.53 mL. The observed table identifies last round's purported 10/1 selection aef4c70d74081b04c15e as m122 at 2/1, so m177's intermediate point remains unmeasured. With matched 2/1, 5/1, and 20/1 observations bef81d4dd93af26c12a9, 76643e968ecc935c745c, and 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7, this directly locates the completion rise.

Measure m177 at 50/1, 150 uL, predicted 21.82/59.36 mL. Its 20/1 completion differs dramatically between 50 and 150 uL: 8.50 versus 57.02 mL (aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 and 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7). The measured 50/1, 50-uL anchor is 21.33/59.88 (5b706e17e8412d02342f). This tests whether the discrepancy extends to weaker eluent or is confined to the 20/1 observation, while completing the selected 150-uL series.

Measure secondary alcohol m60 at 2/1, 50 uL, predicted 11.20/16.76 mL. Its matched 5/1 label was 27.63/36.92 and substantially underpredicted at acquisition (985361f6699d97f9464f). This stronger-eluent point tests whether the revised response rises too early and helps distinguish a localized transition from a general alcohol offset.

Measure methoxybenzyl alcohol m120 at 1/1, 150 uL, predicted 9.19/15.08 mL. Matched 2/1 measured 8.02/10.83 (a5f9f0327623c4752e2e), whereas 5/1 measured 13.90/72.41 (20913a7c2077b80b7351). The predicted strong-eluent reversal and the family's conflicting loading observations warrant a new response segment; this label can constrain where corrections should transfer.

Measure naphthylmethanol m206 at 1/1, 50 uL, predicted 11.23/22.67 mL. Same-protocol pure EA, 2/1, and 5/1 measurements are 6.06/11.87, 12.96/23.61, and 27.80/52.07 (b0f83f107759037eea65, 7c0c324643799c918828, a6145bb0c9947f9515df). This tests the predicted near-plateau from 1/1 to 2/1 and provides a structural contrast to m205's steeper strong-eluent response.

Measure anisaldehyde m118 at 2/1, 100 uL, predicted 6.05/16.88 mL. Its matched 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 observations are 4.78/36.82, 30.17/58.31, and 56.20/117.46 (319e89d7000731f64e7f, fc27fa779102c4aeb8ab, 2d178efe0181baca2bd5). A strong-eluent anchor tests whether the large new weak-eluent correction preserves early onset while allowing completion to respond separately.

Measure sterically crowded acetophenone m29 at 10/1, 50 uL. Its supplied prediction is internally inconsistent: V1 9.19 exceeds V2 7.44 mL. The matched 20/1 observation is 8.64/16.92 (4b104d6f7556c8bc3a51). This label tests the short-interval region underlying that failure and teaches how a crowded carbonyl differs from less substituted acetophenones; the prediction is not evidence of a measured reversal.

Measure para-fluoroacetophenone m34 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 18.16/37.94 mL. Its matched 20/1 anchor is 14.52/32.08 (122ecf89b68742b1bf36). Newly measured para-bromo and para-iodo analogues finish near 51 and 49 mL at 50/1 (605436d35600502e8c2e, 20a5a5008211ea15a65a). Test the predicted shallower fluoro response, with loading mass and the iodide's sample volume retained as covariates.

Measure ortho-bromoacetophenone m43 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 10.74/31.70 mL. Its matched 5/1 observation is 5.01/12.93 (bfabf8894907ce140562), while para-bromoacetophenone measured 24.95/51.05 at 50/1 (605436d35600502e8c2e). This positional-isomer comparison tests the predicted large response difference and whether local carbonyl environment transfers better than halogen identity alone.

Measure 2-bromopropionic acid m45 at 5/1, 100 uL, predicted 11.68/23.87 mL. Matched pure-EA and 20/1 observations are 5.13/8.56 and 26.49/57.16 (fb031b748f1f5a8cc89e, e6605c23fb1943a6b848). This fills a wide solvent gap in an acid scaffold and tests whether the model places its response rise correctly without transferring cinnamic acid's unusual completion pattern indiscriminately.

Measure m45 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 31.67/69.95 mL, paired with the selected 5/1 row at identical loading conditions. The measured 20/1 anchor e6605c23fb1943a6b848 gives 26.49/57.16. This tests the predicted flattening beyond 20/1 and separates a misplaced transition from an underestimated weak-eluent slope.

Measure previously unobserved bis(trifluoromethyl)bromobenzene m155 at 50/1, 50 uL, predicted 5.45/7.87 mL; maximum observed similarity is 0.367. This probes transfer to a fluorinated, non-H-bonding aromatic environment. Pentafluorobenzene nevertheless measured 7.19/23.25 at 50/1 (8fa8d7ec035c6a829dc4), so low polarity alone does not establish the predicted short interval. The structures and loading masses differ.

Measure previously unobserved ortho-chloroiodobenzene m151 at 50/1, 50 uL, predicted 6.65/14.32 mL; maximum observed similarity is 0.333. Pending m157 and m138 provide other iodinated aromatic environments. This adds an ortho mixed-halogen probe to that connected comparison and tests low-retention structural transfer without assuming the pending labels.

Measure dibenzalacetone m164 at 20/1, 100 uL, predicted 11.29/39.20 mL. Matched 1/1 and 50/1 observations are 5.13/10.05 and 28.20/68.68 (3f6b817d855e67b3b406, c9bef93a79964dc6ede1). Related chalcone measured only 6.22/23.00 at 20/1 (a7f8c888870123f3b277). This intermediate label tests how extended conjugation changes onset and completion response rather than presuming a common aromatic-ketone correction.

Measure biphenyl butanone m68 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 14.23/31.38 mL. Its matched 20/1 label is 6.07/17.50 (cb534927304d5c892100), whereas acetylnaphthalene at 50/1 measured 40.62/65.53 (8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49). This tests whether the modest weak-eluent response transfers across extended aromatic ketones; fused versus linked rings, side chain, and loading differences prevent a single-feature causal interpretation.

Measure methyl mandelate m99 at 5/1, 50 uL, predicted 22.80/34.74 mL. Its matched 2/1 anchor is 11.57/15.78 (304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07); at 150 uL, 1/1 and 10/1 measured 5.51/13.41 and 34.78/57.44 (3ef36e4ee22e16660eb4, 7bbdec21c428010dd67b). This tests the intermediate response of an alcohol adjacent to an ester, extending alcohol learning beyond simple arylalkanols while keeping loading differences explicit.

hypotheses.content: Large weak-eluent errors often require a correction to response shape and to the two endpoints separately, rather than a uniform increase across solvent ratios.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Strong- and intermediate-eluent anchors can prevent large late-elution labels from shifting an entire curve and can teach distinct onset and completion responses.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m118 retain early onset at 2/1 after the newly observed large 50/1 completion, and how does its completion connect to 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol solvent responses depend strongly on hydroxyl environment and scaffold. Recent failures include an earlier-than-predicted rise for m60 and much broader completion for nitrophenethyl alcohol, while pure-EA m205 and strong-eluent m119 were reasonably predicted. Loading-sensitive or variable m120 observations remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected comparisons can teach where alcohol corrections transfer and where neighboring ester groups, hydroxyl spacing, or loading conditions change the response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m60, m206, m120, and m99 follow their predicted stronger- or intermediate-eluent segments, or does retraining still misplace the rise?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic carbonyl solvent responses are structure-dependent. Halogen substitution, carbonyl crowding, side chain, ring connectivity, and conjugation can distinguish shallow responses from substantial weak-eluent retention; a common upward correction is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched solvent anchors and connected structural comparisons can distinguish molecule-specific offsets from transferable response features. m29 additionally exposes an endpoint-ordering failure.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted weak-eluent differences among para-fluoro, para-bromo, and ortho-bromo acetophenones real, and do conjugated or linked-ring ketones follow their predicted response growth?

hypotheses.content: m177's very short 20/1 interval does not transfer from 50 to 150 uL. The discrepancy may reflect loading dependence or experimental variability; the 10/1 response remains unmeasured according to the observed table.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The 48.52-mL completion difference at 20/1 is large enough to distort neighboring predictions. A common-loading series and a second cross-loading comparison can clarify the extent of the discrepancy without assigning an unverified mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, does completion rise between 10/1 and 20/1, and does 50/1 agree with the existing 50-uL observation?

hypotheses.content: Carboxylic-acid response patterns may be scaffold- and condition-dependent. m45 may have a conventional rise with weakening eluent, but its sparse anchors do not establish the transition location or the predicted flattening beyond 20/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An additional acid curve can constrain transfer from cinnamic acid's unusual completion behavior to a smaller alpha-bromo acid and related ester chemistry.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed loading, do m45's 5/1 and 50/1 endpoints support the predicted transition and subsequent flattening?

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels reinforce endpoint-specific response repair but weaken any blanket upward correction. m118 at 50/1 was underpredicted by 13.05/39.02 mL, and m200 at 1/1 and 2/1 had completion underpredictions of 19.21 and 35.53 mL. In contrast, m13 at 2/1, m205 in pure EA, m119 at 1/1, m30 at 10/1, and m196 at 50/1 were reasonably predicted. m60 at 5/1 exposed an earlier response rise than forecast. The new m64 labels closely match the shallow response of m65, despite the prior higher weak-eluent prediction, while m35's onset was underpredicted but its completion was close. Several recent CW measurements also showed completion overprediction, including m186, m81, and m92, arguing against selecting only expected high-retention failures. For m177, the 150-uL 20/1 measurement decisively weakens the hypothesis that the short 50-uL interval generalizes across loading. There is also a record discrepancy: recent-outcome prose calls aef4c70d74081b04c15e an m177 10/1 experiment, but the authoritative observed table identifies it as m122 at 2/1, 50 uL. I therefore do not treat its 6.42/10.23 result as evidence for an m177 reversal and select the actual m177 10/1, 150-uL candidate. All errors discussed here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The pending batch already supplies ester and ether response segments, fluorenone comparisons, a phenol intermediate point, and several new iodinated or brominated aromatic structures. These supplements add experiments that discriminate specific remaining explanations: two m177 rows address an unresolved loading discrepancy and the missing intermediate measurement; four alcohol rows test structural transfer and transition placement; m118 supplies a strong-eluent constraint after a large late-elution failure; five carbonyl rows connect positional substitution, halogen identity, crowding, conjugation, and ring connectivity; and the m45 pair resolves a sparsely observed acid curve. Two new aromatic probes test transfer in the low-retention region and connect to pending halogenated compounds. Most nearly identical loading variants were omitted, except where m177's measured discrepancy makes a loading comparison scientifically useful. The batch seeks labels that can improve many related Row predictions, including modest-retention rows, rather than maximizing retention or interval width. Quantile widths are treated as uncalibrated single-predictor outputs; zero lower quantiles, quantile crossings, and occasional endpoint inversions make a width-only ranking unpersuasive. Missing experimental variables and measurement variability limit mechanistic attribution, so comparisons are framed as tests of predictive relationships.
